## Hawaii Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/hawaii.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Hawaii Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Hawaii residents.

Hawaii Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Hawaii's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Haw. R. Civ. P. 60(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (60(b)(1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Hawaii, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundHawaii Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Haw. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Hawaii

Hawaii follows federal extrinsic/intrinsic framework.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Hawaii law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Hawaii, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Hawaii

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Hawaii can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Hawaii

Hawaii's Haw. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Hawaii's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Hawaii

Hawaii stipulated judgments reviewed under contract-law principles.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Hawaii courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Hawaii. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Hawaii Motion

Speed matters in Hawaii. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Haw. R. Civ. P. 60(b), filing beyond 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Hawaii:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Hawaii means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

GroundIdaho Deadline

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

GroundIllinois Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)2 years

Fraud on the court2 years (intrinsic); no limit (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)30 years (void)

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 2 years of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under 735 ILCS 5/2-1401 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Illinois law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Illinois courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

For ordinary relief under Ind. T.R. 60(B), filing beyond 1 year ((1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Indiana:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Indiana means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Iowa Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/iowa.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Iowa Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Iowa residents.

Iowa Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Iowa's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Iowa R. Civ. P. 1.1012. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year. Fraud grounds are more generous in Iowa, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundIowa Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Iowa R. Civ. P. 1.1012 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Iowa

Iowa preserves extrinsic-fraud action via independent petition.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Iowa law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Iowa, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Iowa

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Iowa can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Iowa

Iowa's Iowa R. Civ. P. 1.1012 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Iowa's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Iowa

Iowa stipulated judgments final absent fraud, duress, or mutual mistake.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Iowa courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Iowa. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Iowa Motion

Speed matters in Iowa. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Iowa R. Civ. P. 1.1012, filing beyond 1 year is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Iowa:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Iowa means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Kansas Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/kansas.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Kansas Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Kansas residents.

Kansas Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Kansas's primary motion-to-vacate rule is K.S.A. 60-260(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (60-260(b)(1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Kansas, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundKansas Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (60-260(b)(1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (60-260(b)(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under K.S.A. 60-260(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Kansas

Kansas preserves independent extrinsic-fraud action.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Kansas law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Kansas, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Kansas

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Kansas can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Kansas

Kansas's K.S.A. 60-260(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Kansas's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Kansas

Kansas stipulated judgments require showing fraud or mutual mistake.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Kansas courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Kansas. See default vs consent judgments.

Kansas Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Kansas, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Kansas debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 40,849 consumer bankruptcy cases from Kansas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 718,67399.4%0.5%

Chapter 1322,17673.1%26.9%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Kansas Motion

Speed matters in Kansas. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under K.S.A. 60-260(b), filing beyond 1 year (60-260(b)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

## Kentucky Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/kentucky.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Kentucky Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Kentucky residents.

Kentucky Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Kentucky's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Ky. CR 60.02. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (60.02(a-c)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Kentucky, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundKentucky Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (60.02(a-c))

Fraud1 year for perjury/falsified evidence (60.02(c)); reasonable time for other fraud (60.02(d))

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)no fixed limit in Kentucky courts (60.02(e))

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (60.02(a-c)) of the judgment. The rule's text says motions on the remaining grounds must come within a "reasonable time," but Kentucky courts treat a void judgment as a legal nullity that can be attacked whenever it is discovered. Don't sit on a known defect anyway; the safest void motion is a prompt one.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Kentucky

Kentucky writes the distinction into the rule itself: CR 60.02(c) covers perjury or falsified evidence (intrinsic fraud, subject to the 1-year limit), while CR 60.02(d) covers "fraud affecting the proceedings, other than perjury or falsified evidence" (extrinsic fraud, subject only to the reasonable-time standard).

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Kentucky law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Kentucky, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Kentucky

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Kentucky state court can be attacked at any time and are void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

Federal court is different as of 2026. In Coney Island Auto Parts Unlimited, Inc. v. Burton, 607 U.S. ___ (decided January 20, 2026), the Supreme Court held that a void-judgment motion under FRCP 60(b)(4) must still be filed within a "reasonable time" under Rule 60(c)(1). That case arose from a bankruptcy adversary proceeding with defective mail service, so it applies directly to bankruptcy-court judgments. It does not bind Kentucky state courts, but it is one more reason to move quickly once you learn of a service defect.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Kentucky

Kentucky's Ky. CR 60.02 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Kentucky's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Kentucky

Kentucky treats stipulated judgments as final absent fraud, mutual mistake, or similar grounds.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Kentucky courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Kentucky. See default vs consent judgments.

Kentucky Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Kentucky, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Kentucky debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,692 consumer bankruptcy cases from Kentucky's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 731897.5%1.7%

Chapter 131,37472.1%27.0%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Kentucky Motion

Speed matters in Kentucky. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Ky. CR 60.02, filing beyond 1 year (60.02(a-c)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Kentucky:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Kentucky means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Louisiana Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/louisiana.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Louisiana Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Louisiana residents.

Louisiana Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Louisiana's primary motion-to-vacate rule is La. Code Civ. Proc. Art. 2002-2004. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (2004 fraud). Fraud grounds are more generous in Louisiana, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundLouisiana Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (2004 fraud)

Fraud on the court1 year; no limit (void)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (2004 fraud) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under La. Code Civ. Proc. Art. 2002-2004 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Louisiana

Louisiana's Art. 2004 provides liberal fraud remedy distinct from federal Throckmorton.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Louisiana law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Louisiana, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Louisiana

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Louisiana can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(5) satisfied judgment

Louisiana's unique nullity action (Art. 2002) allows broad attack on vices of form/substance.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Louisiana courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Louisiana. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Louisiana Motion

Speed matters in Louisiana. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under La. Code Civ. Proc. Art. 2002-2004, filing beyond 1 year (2004 fraud) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

## Maryland Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/maryland.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Maryland Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Maryland residents.

Maryland Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Maryland's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Md. Rule 2-535. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 30 days (ordinary); no limit (fraud/irregularity). Fraud grounds are more generous in Maryland, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundMaryland Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)30 days (ordinary); no limit (fraud/irregularity)

Fraud on the courtno fixed limit (fraud)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 30 days (ordinary); no limit (fraud/irregularity) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Md. Rule 2-535 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Maryland

Maryland retains extrinsic-fraud doctrine via independent action in equity.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Maryland law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Maryland, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Maryland

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Maryland can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Maryland

Maryland's Md. Rule 2-535 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Maryland's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Maryland

Maryland's 30-day revisory window is short for ordinary relief.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Maryland courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Maryland. See default vs consent judgments.

Maryland Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Maryland, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Maryland debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 559 consumer bankruptcy cases from Maryland's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 742097.4%0.0%

Chapter 13139n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Maryland Motion

Speed matters in Maryland. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Md. Rule 2-535, filing beyond 30 days (ordinary); no limit (fraud/irregularity) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Maryland:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Maryland means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Massachusetts Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/massachusetts.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Massachusetts Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Massachusetts residents.

Massachusetts Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Massachusetts's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Mass. R. Civ. P. 60(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (60(b)(1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Massachusetts, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundMassachusetts Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (60(b)(1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Mass. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Massachusetts

MA follows federal Chavez v. New England Mut. Life extrinsic-fraud doctrine.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Massachusetts law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Massachusetts, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Massachusetts

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Massachusetts can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Massachusetts

Massachusetts's Mass. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Massachusetts's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Massachusetts

Massachusetts stipulated judgments reviewed under contract principles.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Massachusetts courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Massachusetts. See default vs consent judgments.

Massachusetts Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Massachusetts, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Massachusetts debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,356 consumer bankruptcy cases from Massachusetts's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 71,29098.3%0.9%

Chapter 136659.1%40.9%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Massachusetts Motion

Speed matters in Massachusetts. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Mass. R. Civ. P. 60(b), filing beyond 1 year (60(b)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Massachusetts:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Massachusetts means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (74.06(b)(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Mo. R. Civ. P. 74.06 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Missouri

Missouri preserves extrinsic-fraud action via independent equity proceeding.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Missouri law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Missouri, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Missouri

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Missouri can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Missouri

Missouri's Mo. R. Civ. P. 74.06 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Missouri's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Missouri

Missouri stipulated judgments enforced under contract principles.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Missouri courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Missouri. See default vs consent judgments.

Missouri Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Missouri, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Missouri debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 45,771 consumer bankruptcy cases from Missouri's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 722,13299.0%0.8%

Chapter 1323,63955.1%44.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Missouri Motion

Speed matters in Missouri. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Mo. R. Civ. P. 74.06, filing beyond 1 year (74.06(b)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Missouri:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Missouri means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Montana Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/montana.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Montana Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Montana residents.

Montana Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Montana's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Mont. R. Civ. P. 60(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 60 days (60(b)(1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Montana, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundMontana Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)60 days (60(b)(1-3))

Fraud on the court60 days (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 60 days (60(b)(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Mont. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Montana

Montana follows federal extrinsic-fraud doctrine.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Montana law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Montana, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Montana

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Montana can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Montana

Montana's Mont. R. Civ. P. 60(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Montana's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Montana

Montana's 60-day window is one of the shortest in the Rockies.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Montana courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Montana. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Montana Motion

Speed matters in Montana. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Mont. R. Civ. P. 60(b), filing beyond 60 days (60(b)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Montana:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Montana means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Nebraska Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/nebraska.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Nebraska Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nebraska residents.

Nebraska Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Nebraska's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-2001. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within term of court (ordinary). Fraud grounds are more generous in Nebraska, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundNebraska Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)term of court (ordinary)

Fraud on the court1 year (fraud)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within term of court (ordinary) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-2001 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

Nebraska's 'term of court' framework is unique; stipulated judgments fully binding absent fraud.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Nebraska courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Chapter 757100.0%0.0%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Speed matters in Nebraska. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in New Jersey

NJ stipulated judgments reviewed under contract-law fraud standards.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. New Jersey courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in New Jersey. See default vs consent judgments.

New Jersey Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in New Jersey, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how New Jersey debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,580 consumer bankruptcy cases from New Jersey's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 752697.3%2.7%

Chapter 131,05431.0%68.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your New Jersey Motion

Speed matters in New Jersey. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under N.J. Ct. R. 4:50-1, filing beyond 1 year ((a-c)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In New Jersey:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, New Jersey means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## New Mexico Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/new-mexico.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

New Mexico Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New Mexico residents.

New Mexico Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

New Mexico's primary motion-to-vacate rule is NMRA 1-060(B). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year ((1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in New Mexico, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundNew Mexico Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year ((1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year ((1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under NMRA 1-060(B) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in New Mexico

NM follows federal extrinsic-fraud doctrine.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under New Mexico law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in New Mexico, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in New Mexico

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in New Mexico can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for New Mexico

New Mexico's NMRA 1-060(B) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

New Mexico's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in New Mexico

New Mexico stipulated judgments final absent fraud or mutual mistake.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. New Mexico courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in New Mexico. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your New Mexico Motion

Speed matters in New Mexico. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under NMRA 1-060(B), filing beyond 1 year ((1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In New Mexico:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, New Mexico means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## New York Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/new-york.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

New York Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

New York Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

New York's primary motion-to-vacate rule is CPLR 5015. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (5015(a)(1)). Fraud grounds are more generous in New York, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundNew York Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (5015(a)(1))

Fraud on the courtreasonable time (5015(a)(3) fraud)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time (5015(a)(4))

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (5015(a)(1)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under CPLR 5015 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in New York

New York preserves extrinsic-fraud doctrine via plenary action.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under New York law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in New York, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in New York

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in New York can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for New York

New York's CPLR 5015 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

New York's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in New York

NY CPLR 5015(a)(3) provides broad fraud remedy; stipulated judgments reviewable under Hallock v. State.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. New York courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in New York. See default vs consent judgments.

New York Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in New York, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how New York debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,231 consumer bankruptcy cases from New York's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 71,14598.7%1.2%

Chapter 138628.2%71.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your New York Motion

Speed matters in New York. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under CPLR 5015, filing beyond 1 year (5015(a)(1)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In New York:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, New York means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Ohio R. Civ. P. 60(B), filing beyond 1 year (60(B)(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Ohio:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Ohio means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Oklahoma Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/oklahoma.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Oklahoma Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oklahoma residents.

Oklahoma Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Oklahoma's primary motion-to-vacate rule is 12 O.S. 1031. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 2 years (fraud). Fraud grounds are more generous in Oklahoma, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundOklahoma Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)2 years (fraud)

Fraud on the court2 years

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 2 years (fraud) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under 12 O.S. 1031 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Oklahoma

Oklahoma preserves extrinsic-fraud doctrine via 1031(4) petition.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Oklahoma law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Oklahoma, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Oklahoma

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Oklahoma can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Oklahoma

Oklahoma's 12 O.S. 1031 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Oklahoma's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Oklahoma

Oklahoma 1031 petition provides broad relief on enumerated statutory grounds.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Oklahoma courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Oklahoma. See default vs consent judgments.

Oklahoma Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Oklahoma, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Oklahoma debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 112 consumer bankruptcy cases from Oklahoma's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711099.1%0.9%

Chapter 132n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Oklahoma Motion

Speed matters in Oklahoma. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under 12 O.S. 1031, filing beyond 2 years (fraud) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Oklahoma:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Oklahoma means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Oregon Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/oregon.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Oregon Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oregon residents.

Oregon Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Oregon's primary motion-to-vacate rule is ORCP 71. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year (B(1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Oregon, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundOregon Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year (B(1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year (B(1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under ORCP 71 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Oregon

Oregon preserves independent extrinsic-fraud action.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Oregon law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Oregon, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Oregon can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(5) satisfied judgment

Oregon stipulated judgments reviewed under Stevens v. Horton contract principles.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Oregon courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Oregon. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Oregon Motion

Speed matters in Oregon. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under ORCP 71, filing beyond 1 year (B(1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

## Pennsylvania Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/pennsylvania.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Pennsylvania Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Pennsylvania residents.

Pennsylvania Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Pennsylvania's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Pa. R. Civ. P. 3051, 42 Pa.C.S. 5505. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 30 days (5505 ordinary). Fraud grounds are more generous in Pennsylvania, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundPennsylvania Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)30 days (5505 ordinary)

Fraud on the courtreasonable time (fraud)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 30 days (5505 ordinary) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Pa. R. Civ. P. 3051, 42 Pa.C.S. 5505 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Pennsylvania preserves extrinsic-fraud action via petition to open/strike.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Pennsylvania law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

PA's 30-day modification window is tight; post-30 day relief requires fraud or void judgment.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Pennsylvania courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Pennsylvania. See default vs consent judgments.

Pennsylvania Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Pennsylvania, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Pennsylvania debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,513 consumer bankruptcy cases from Pennsylvania's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7415n/an/a

Chapter 131,098n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Pennsylvania Motion

Speed matters in Pennsylvania. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Pa. R. Civ. P. 3051, 42 Pa.C.S. 5505, filing beyond 30 days (5505 ordinary) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.
