## South Dakota Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/south-dakota.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

South Dakota Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for South Dakota residents.

South Dakota Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

South Dakota's primary motion-to-vacate rule is SDCL 15-6-60(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year ((1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in South Dakota, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundSouth Dakota Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year ((1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year ((1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under SDCL 15-6-60(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in South Dakota

SD follows federal extrinsic-fraud framework.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under South Dakota law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in South Dakota, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in South Dakota

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in South Dakota can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for South Dakota

South Dakota's SDCL 15-6-60(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

South Dakota's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in South Dakota

SD stipulated judgments final absent fraud or mutual mistake.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. South Dakota courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in South Dakota. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your South Dakota Motion

Speed matters in South Dakota. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under SDCL 15-6-60(b), filing beyond 1 year ((1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In South Dakota:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, South Dakota means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Tennessee Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/tennessee.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Tennessee Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Tennessee residents.

Tennessee Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Tennessee's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Tenn. R. Civ. P. 60.02. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year ((1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Tennessee, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundTennessee Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year ((1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year ((1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Tenn. R. Civ. P. 60.02 is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Tennessee

Tennessee preserves extrinsic-fraud action under Brown v. Weik.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Tennessee law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Tennessee, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Tennessee

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Tennessee can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Tennessee

Tennessee's Tenn. R. Civ. P. 60.02 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Tennessee's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Tennessee

TN stipulated judgments final absent fraud or mutual mistake.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Tennessee courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Tennessee. See default vs consent judgments.

Tennessee Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Tennessee, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Tennessee debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,840 consumer bankruptcy cases from Tennessee's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 758995.5%4.5%

Chapter 131,25117.3%82.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Speed matters in Tennessee. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

## Texas Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/texas.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Texas Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Texas residents.

Texas Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Texas's primary motion-to-vacate rule is Tex. R. Civ. P. 329b; bill of review. Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 30 days (plenary); 2 years (bill of review). Fraud grounds are more generous in Texas, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundTexas Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)30 days (plenary); 2 years (bill of review)

Fraud on the courtno time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)no time (void)

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 30 days (plenary); 2 years (bill of review) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under Tex. R. Civ. P. 329b; bill of review is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Texas

Texas preserves robust extrinsic-fraud doctrine via bill of review; intrinsic fraud barred.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Texas law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Texas, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Texas

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Texas can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Texas

Texas's Tex. R. Civ. P. 329b; bill of review is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Texas's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Texas

TX's 30-day plenary window; bill of review requires Craddock factors + prevented-defense showing.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Texas courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Texas. See default vs consent judgments.

Texas Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Texas, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Texas debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 30,781 consumer bankruptcy cases from Texas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711,84497.8%2.0%

Chapter 1318,93736.8%63.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Texas Motion

Speed matters in Texas. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Tex. R. Civ. P. 329b; bill of review, filing beyond 30 days (plenary); 2 years (bill of review) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Texas:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Texas means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Virginia can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

FRCP 60 State Analog for Virginia

Virginia's Va. Code 8.01-428 is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Virginia's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

Stipulated Judgments in Virginia

Virginia's 21-day plenary window is among the shortest; post-21 day limited to statutory grounds.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Virginia courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Virginia. See default vs consent judgments.

Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

When a judgment cannot be vacated in Virginia, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts collection and discharges the underlying debt. These FJC numbers show how Virginia debtors use the bankruptcy remedy when state-court relief is unavailable.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,064 consumer bankruptcy cases from Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7514n/an/a

Chapter 1355071.2%28.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Timeline for Filing Your Virginia Motion

Speed matters in Virginia. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under Va. Code 8.01-428, filing beyond 21 days (plenary); 2 years (fraud) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

When Bankruptcy Is the Cleaner Path

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Virginia:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Virginia means test, and judgment after bankruptcy.

## Washington Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]
Source: https://vacatejudgment.org/states/washington.html

← vacatejudgment.org home

Washington Motion to Vacate Judgment: Deadlines and Grounds [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Washington residents.

Washington Motion-to-Vacate Deadlines

Washington's primary motion-to-vacate rule is CR 60(b). Ordinary grounds (mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect) must generally be raised within 1 year ((1-3)). Fraud grounds are more generous in Washington, and void-judgment attacks have no fixed time limit.

GroundWashington Deadline

Ordinary relief (mistake/neglect)1 year ((1-3))

Fraud on the court1 year (intrinsic); reasonable time (extrinsic)

Void judgment (jurisdiction/service)void any time

If your motion targets the ordinary window, it must be filed within 1 year ((1-3)) of the judgment. A void-judgment attack under CR 60(b) is not time-barred because the judgment was never valid to begin with.

Extrinsic vs Intrinsic Fraud in Washington

Washington follows federal extrinsic-fraud doctrine.

The distinction matters because extrinsic fraud (fraud that prevented you from presenting your case) typically can be attacked at any reasonable time under Washington law, often via an independent equity proceeding. Intrinsic fraud (false evidence or perjury within the case) is usually bound by the ordinary window.

Extrinsic examples: opposing party intentionally concealed your address to prevent service; bribed your lawyer; kept you from testifying.

Intrinsic examples: perjured affidavit of amount owed; forged signed contract; false account statement.

If you have evidence of extrinsic fraud in Washington, you likely have a cause of action even after the ordinary vacatur window has closed.

Void Judgments - No Time Limit in Washington

A judgment is void (not merely voidable) when the court lacked:

Personal jurisdiction - e.g., improper service, out-of-state defendant with insufficient minimum contacts.

Subject-matter jurisdiction - e.g., state-court suit on exclusively federal claim.

Due process compliance - e.g., no meaningful notice or opportunity to be heard.

Void judgments in Washington can be attacked at any time and should be void as of their entry. Service defects (sewer service, no personal service attempt before publication, substitute service on someone not authorized) are by far the most common basis.

Washington's CR 60(b) is the state analog of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60 (or FRCP 60(b) for relief from final judgments). In federal practice, FRCP 60(b) covers:

(1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect

(2) newly discovered evidence

(3) fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct

(4) void judgment

(5) satisfied judgment

(6) any other reason that justifies relief

Washington's rule tracks this structure with variations noted above. If your case is in federal court (e.g., bankruptcy adversary proceeding), FRCP 60(b) applies directly, and after Coney Island Auto Parts v. Burton (2026) even a 60(b)(4) void-judgment motion must be filed within a reasonable time.

WA stipulated judgments reviewed under White v. Holm four-factor test.

Stipulated (consent) judgments are harder to vacate because they represent a contractual agreement. Washington courts generally require a showing of:

Fraud. The other party lied about a material fact you relied on.

Mutual mistake. Both parties were wrong about a material fact (e.g., amount owed was misstated).

Duress or coercion. You signed under improper pressure or threat.

Lack of capacity or authority. You could not legally consent, or the signing attorney lacked authority.

Ordinary remorse or change of mind will not vacate a stipulated judgment in Washington. See default vs consent judgments.

Timeline for Filing Your Washington Motion

Speed matters in Washington. The typical timeline:

Day 0. Judgment entered (or discovered by you).

Day 1-14. Gather evidence - service records, correspondence, affidavits, meritorious defense documents.

Day 15-30. Draft motion with supporting affidavit. Courts view delay as waiver.

Day 30+. File motion, serve opposing party. Ask for a hearing.

For ordinary relief under CR 60(b), filing beyond 1 year ((1-3)) is fatal. Use our motion template to stay ahead of the deadline.

If the motion-to-vacate window has closed or your grounds are weak, bankruptcy remains effective. In Washington:

Chapter 7 discharges the underlying debt within 90-120 days.

Chapter 13 restructures the judgment debt over 3-5 years.

Section 522(f) judicial lien avoidance strips judgment liens that impair exemptions.

Section 362 automatic stay halts all collection activity on filing.
